extracted.intended_audience: legislators, statesmen, and the educated public concerned with constitutional and political reform (late 18th-century European/British readership)
extracted.subtask_description: A polemical analysis of a revolutionary constitution and its practical effects on military discipline, municipal power, and public finance. The text outlines standards for stable government institutions and prudent fiscal administration, warning against reforms that undermine authority or create faction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Army must act only as an instrument
rubrics_metrics.description: The army should 'never act but as an instrument' and must not 'erect[] itself into a deliberate body' acting on its own resolutions; otherwise 'the government...will immediately degenerate into a military democracy.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid institutional arrangements or doctrines that encourage the army to deliberate or form independent assemblies; maintain the army's role as subordinate to civil authority to prevent a 'political monster' that consumes its creators.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition of soldiers' irregular consultations and democratic assemblies
rubrics_metrics.description: Irregular consultations and turbulent committees formed by common soldiers and non-commissioned officers (seditious committees, 'comices') are dangerous and undermine discipline.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not tolerate grassroots military assemblies that act without or against officers' authority; such bodies substitute mutiny for discipline and threaten national stability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Personal, vigorous authority at the head of the army
rubrics_metrics.description: The supreme command must be 'a real, vigorous, effective, decided, personal authority' — a nominal or impotent head (a 'cipher') cannot secure military obedience.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure the army's supreme commander inspires gratitude or fear and has effective, personal authority; avoid diffuse or merely nominal command structures that cannot enforce discipline.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limit municipal authority over troops to requisition only
rubrics_metrics.description: Municipalities must not 'break the officers, try them, give orders to the soldiers, drive them from the posts...or enslave the troops to the caprice' of towns; the Assembly's decrees only authorized requisition, not municipal command.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Legally and practically confine municipal powers vis-à-vis military forces to narrow administrative rights (e.g., requisition), preventing towns from exercising direct command or judicial powers over soldiers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid mixing soldiers with municipal clubs and civic feasting
rubrics_metrics.description: Royal circulars encouraging regiments to join clubs and municipal entertainments will 'make them admirable citizens after the French mode, but not quite so good soldiers' and risk weakening military subordination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not institutionalize civic fraternization that merges military and municipal identities; social integration with politicized local societies can convert soldiers into partisan actors and erode obedience.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clear, unambiguous seat of military patronage and promotion
rubrics_metrics.description: Ambiguous promotion (double negotiation with court and Assembly) will 'promote faction' and 'poison the corps of officers'; unclear patronage makes officers pursue factional influence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design appointment and promotion systems that have a single, transparent seat of authority (or other clear, consistent rules) to avoid factions and political bargaining within the officer corps.

rubrics_metrics.name: Risks of elective selection of officers
rubrics_metrics.description: Giving soldiers negative or elective power over officers undermines the king's authority and the chain of command; soldiers will naturally prefer elective arrangements seen elsewhere (municipalities, justices, etc.).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid elective mechanisms for choosing military commanders; preserve the officer-soldier relationship by preventing rank selection from becoming a popular or municipal franchise.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid instilling civic rights that conflict with military subordination
rubrics_metrics.description: Teaching soldiers the 'rights of man' (that they are citizens with rights) leads them to think they should choose where highest obedience is due, thereby eroding obedience to officers and sovereign.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be cautious in applying broad civic doctrines to active military personnel; maintain a distinction between civic rights and the special duties and subordination required of soldiers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assembly's ephemeral duration makes it unfit to command armies
rubrics_metrics.description: An Assembly with only a short continuance ('two years') is an unstable organ to promote obedience in an army whose officers would face a transient and uncertain authority.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Entrust long-term military command and policy to stable institutions or persons with continuity; ephemeral representative bodies should not wield sole, decisive military authority.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use effective punitive measures and inquiries to check military disorder
rubrics_metrics.description: When commandants are murdered or troops trample decrees, expected remedies are courts (civil and martial), breaking or decimating corps, and serious inquiries — not merely more decrees or proclamations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Respond to military insubordination with concrete legal and disciplinary action (investigations, courts-martial, appropriate punishments) rather than repeated proclamations or oaths.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid relying on oaths and proclamations as sole remedy
rubrics_metrics.description: Renewing decrees and multiplying oaths (even 'prêtés avec la plus imposante solennité') are insufficient and may weaken religious sanctions; ceremonial oaths are poor substitutes for effective authority.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not expect ritualistic or rhetorical measures (oaths, proclamations) to restore discipline — pair legal/administrative action with moral persuasion and enforceable sanctions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Municipal armies must not be independent democratic monsters
rubrics_metrics.description: A municipal army that is a 'mere democratic body, unconnected with the crown or the kingdom' becomes a monster when related to crown, Assembly, tribunals, or other armies, likely producing national calamity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Integrate local/militias into a coherent national military framework; avoid autonomous district forces whose loyalties and structures conflict with national command and legal order.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid engineering systems that create reciprocal institutional debility
rubrics_metrics.description: Flaws in one constitutional part (crown, assembly, military, municipalities) expose and worsen defects in others; remedies must consider reciprocal relations rather than isolated fixes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Treat institutional reform holistically: do not attempt piecemeal reforms (e.g., curb crown without strengthening corresponding civil institutions) that leave gaps exploited by faction or force.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sound fiscal management: secure ample revenue
rubrics_metrics.description: A financier's first object is 'to secure an ample revenue' — the revenue is 'the spring of all power' and fundamental to public virtue and the state's capacities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure the state has sufficient and sustainable revenue streams before undertaking major reforms; revenue enables magnanimity, public works, and the exercise of public virtue.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sound fiscal management: impose taxes with judgment and equality
rubrics_metrics.description: Taxes should be imposed 'with judgment and equality' so as to be fair and politically sustainable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design tax policy that balances equity and efficiency, avoiding arbitrary or vindictive impositions that provoke popular resistance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sound fiscal management: employ revenue economically
rubrics_metrics.description: Public funds must be 'employed...economically' to maximize benefit and maintain public trust.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Practice frugality, prioritize expenditures, and avoid wasteful or ostentatious spending that undermines long-term fiscal health.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sound fiscal management: if using credit, secure its foundations
rubrics_metrics.description: When use of credit is necessary, secure its foundations 'by the clearness and candor of his proceedings, the exactness of his calculations, and the solidity of his funds.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When borrowing, present transparent accounts, rigorous calculations, and credible revenue plans to maintain creditors' confidence and avoid speculative mismanagement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consistency between political declarations and practical coercion
rubrics_metrics.description: Declaring rights (e.g., 'troops ought not to fire on citizens') while planning to use troops against subjects (colonies, peasants) is hypocritical and destabilizing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Align political principles with practice; do not promulgate universal rights and then rely on force to enforce policies that contradict those rights, as this erodes legitimacy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid legislator self-interest in property confiscation and protection
rubrics_metrics.description: Legislators who have acquired confiscated lands have an interest to preserve marketable property and will selectively protect or abrogate property rights, undermining consistent legal principles.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prevent conflicts of interest in reforming property regimes; avoid ad hoc protections that create insecurity and appear self-serving, as property insecurity breeds unrest.

rubrics_metrics.name: Maintain a balanced relation between private wealth and public collection
rubrics_metrics.description: The prosperity of nations 'will continue to grow' when a due reciprocal proportion exists between what is left to individuals and what is collected for state efforts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design fiscal systems that preserve incentives for private industriousness while securing adequate public resources — aim for a stable balance, not arbitrary confiscation.
